question.text: Suppose that the angular velocity of rotation of the Earth is increased. Then, as a consequence,

options.text: weight of the object, everywhere on the earth, will decrease.
weight of the object, everywhere on the earth, will increase.
except at poles, weight of the object on the earth, will decrease.
there will be no change in weight anywhere on the earth.

solution.text: Effective acceleration due to gravity, <math><msup><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>-</mo><msup><mrow><mi>ω</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi>R</mi><mrow><mrow><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">cos</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, where <math><mi>ϕ</mi></math> is latitude. There will be no change in gravity at poles as <math><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mn>90</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>o</mi></mrow></msup></math>. At other points as <math><mi>ω</mi></math> increases, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>'</mo></math> will decrease.
